newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ labour costs up 2.4 pct in year to Dec '96 qtr.
newsitem.headline: NZ labour costs up 2.4 pct in year to Dec '96 qtr.

text.p: New Zealand labour costs increased by 2.4 percent from the December 1995 quarter to the December 1996 quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Friday.
This followed increases of 2.3 percent and 2.5 percent for the years to June and September 1996.
"Labour costs rose by 2.8 percent in the public sector and and by 2.3 percent in the private sector from the December 1995 quarter to the December 1996 quarter," SNZ said.

In the year to December 1996, salary and wage rates rose by 2.0 percent. Non-wage labour costs increased by 4.5 percent, with private sector costs rising 4.7 percent and public sector costs going up 4.0 percent, SNZ said.

From the September 1996 quarter to the December 1996 quarter, labour costs rose by 0.6 percent overall, with salary and wage rates (including overtime) rising 0.7 percent and non-wage labour costs increasing by 0.8 percent.
SNZ said the slightly lower overall movement was caused by index number rounding.

The increase in salary and wage rates (up 2.0 percent) accounted for 68 percent of the 2.4 percent annual increase in labour costs, with the remaining 32 percent coming from higher non-wage labour costs (up 4.5 percent).

An increase in ACC (Accident Compensation Corporation) employer premium costs accounted for 19 percent of the latest overall annual increae in labour costs, while higher annual leave and statutory holiday costs accounted for 11 percent, SNZ said.
Employee participation in employer-subsidised superannuation schemes fell in the latest quarter, resuming the downward trend evident since the series started in the December 1992 quarter.
Participation continued to fall in the public sector. There was a small fall in participation in the private sector, following an increase, the first to be recorded, in the September quarter.
